CarDS Lab Presentation
LATENT-RCT: learned representations for confounding control in target trial emulation
15 October 2026

Does X cause Y?

Ceteris paribus: all other things being equal

But RCTs are

  1. Costly
  2. Slow
  3. Often exclude multimorbid and underrepresented patients

Propensity scores balance only what is measured

  1. Missingness: real-world EHR data are incomplete
  2. Missing physiology: LV function, congestion, atrial substrate
  3. Hard to operationalize: codes differ across systems

The goal of LATENT-RCT is to bring unstructured information into trial emulation.

More: A1 · Trial selection · A2 · Emulation-quality criteria · A3 · All 38 trials (Table 1)

No PS contains any echocardiographic measurement. PS-Clinical without LVEF was re-imputed without LVEF, with 5 draws: per-item |SMD| is averaged across draws and HRs are combined by Rubin's rules.

ECG representation

BCL self-supervised signal encoder, 256-d → 32 PCs computed within each trial cohort. Latest 12-lead ECG in [index − 365 d, index], index day included (37% of ECGs, version 1 cohorts; disclosed per trial).

Placebo

Permuted ECG: the embeddings are shuffled between patients within each trial, so the dimension is the same and the information is gone.

PS and matching

L2-penalised logistic PS on standardised covariates, fixed C = 1 for every specification. 1:1 greedy nearest-neighbour matching on the PS logit, caliper 0.2 SD, without replacement. Sensitivities: caliper 0.1, 1:3 matching, IPTW, overlap weights, gradient-boosted PS. A cell with <11 matched pairs counts as failed.

Rules: mask any held-out item that is the same quantity as, derived from, or in the same code family as a PS input, or has pooled |ρ| ≥ 0.80 with one. Soft proxies (0.50 ≤ |ρ| < 0.80, e.g. BUN, LVESVi, GLS) stay in. Items that are PS inputs are always masked.

Endpoints and tests

  • Primary: relative reduction in mean |SMD| after matching = 1 − (mean over trials with the ECG / without it); 95% CI from 4,000 bootstrap resamples of trials
  • Items are used only where they are observed in both compared cells
  • Secondary endpoints: % of items with |SMD| < 0.1; trials improved; per-domain reductions
  • Exact sign-flip permutation across trials (one-sided vs base or placebo); BH-FDR within families
  • Agreement (secondary): Cox model in the matched cohort, pair-clustered; |Δ log HR| vs the RCT; benchmark-permutation test (RCT results reassigned across trials, 20,000 draws) required for any agreement claim

More: A2 · Emulation-quality criteria
PS-DemoPS-Demo + ECGPS-CVD5PS-CVD5 + ECGECG onlyPermuted ECG only
  • Real covariates, ECGs and follow-up; treatment simulated from the hidden confounder C (LVEF, NT-proBNP, BMI or eGFR; clinically oriented); true HR 0.80; 107 trial × C cells, 50 replicates each
  • C is in no PS except the oracle (93.7% removed)
  • The ECG removes a further 11.3% of the bias that PS-CVD5 leaves (LVEF 15.2% · NT-proBNP 15.1% · BMI 19.2% · eGFR 2.5%)
  • 95% CI coverage: unmatched 51.2%, PS-CVD5 64.8%, PS-CVD5 + ECG 69.2%, oracle 94.4%. No representation substitutes for measuring C
PS-CVD5 analog + ECG + permuted ECG

7 cardiovascular trials + PEPTIC (negative control). PS-CVD5 analog = demographics + HTN, T2D, CAD, AF, HF from earlier admissions. 26 held-out labs, vitals, ventilation and utilisation items (no echo).

Bootstrap CI: 2,000 resamples (seed 0, the v20 convention). The estimate moves by about ±5 points between near-identical specifications.

  1. The ECG improves held-out balance when the PS is thin (demographics and a few diagnoses): PS-CVD5 + ECG 8.8% (4.4 to 13.3) on paper 1's 32 trials (PS-Demo + ECG 11.3%). It beats its permuted placebo (8.0%).
  2. The gain is smaller with richer PS: PS-CVD10 + ECG 5.0%, hdPS + ECG 7.6%, PS-Clinical (no LVEF; 5-draw MI) + ECG 3.2% (−1.0 to 7.2), concentrated in observed LVEF and echo structure.
  3. No trial-specific agreement with the RCTs for PS-CVD5 + ECG: benchmark-permutation P ≥ 0.68 in the 32, all 38 and the 29-trial set. (CVD10 + ECG gave P = .003 on the 32: post hoc, exploratory only.)
  4. Supporting: the plasmode (the ECG removes part of a hidden physiological confounder's bias beyond PS-CVD5) and MIMIC-IV (similar balance gain, no agreement gain).
  5. Caveats: one health system; quality tiers graded post hoc with LLM-assisted raters (clinician review pending); post hoc switch of the primary to PS-CVD5; the return to version 1 cohorts was decided after the fixed-cohort results were known (fixed cohorts: 6.6%; both reported).
More: A6 · Design history
  1. Clinician review of the v19 emulation-quality tiers and the physiologic trial labels (both LLM-assisted so far).
  2. PS-Clinical (no LVEF), 5-draw MI on version 1 cohorts: review the result (3.2%, P = .075 on the 32) and the unstable PS-alone HRs across draws; decide whether to add "was measured" flags.
  3. Disclosure of the post hoc decisions: PS-CVD5 as primary; return to version 1 cohorts after the fixed-cohort results; spec-v2 fixes and framework v2.0 as sensitivities.
  4. Known version 1 cohort issues (COMET metoprolol formulation and LVEF, EMPEROR-Preserved DPP-4i agents, class washouts, LIFE ECG-LVH, TRANSFORM-HF time zero): limitation text, or targeted rebuilds.
  5. Plasmode re-check on the final trial set (pipeline.md §8, pending).
  1. CLMBR-T: back on the aims slide; how and where its results return (main text vs supplement), to be confirmed with the PI.
  2. External validation scope: UK Biobank and dbGaP trial cohorts (ACCORD, WHI, CHS) are planned, not started.
  3. Study name LATENT-RCT (for now): "RCT" may be read as a randomized-trial label by journals and indexers (alternative: LATENT-TTE).
  4. Manuscript file (paper.md vs paper2.md) and the methods lock (pipeline.md §10–11).
More: A6 · Design history

How the 99 candidates were assembled (three waves)

WaveSource of candidatesEmulated
1. DevelopmentLandmark cardiovascular trials and investigator review (63 unique candidates after collapsing design variants)18 (analytic approach developed here)
2. v1.7, prespecifiedList drawn largely from RCT-DUPLICATE, plus investigator scouting (8 further candidates)15 (specs, benchmarks and plan committed before any result)
3. v1.8, prespecifiedAF scouting (28 candidates); the AF hypothesis arose from a post hoc wave-2 pattern5

Counting rule: one RCT = one candidate; design variants of a trial count once, grouped screening entries count separately: 63 + 8 + 28 = 99. Ambiguous groupings (a peri-procedural group; PARTNER 2A/3) give a defensible range of 99–104 (manuscript audit 2026-10-01).

Coverage check: PRISMA-style structured search (2026-10-13)

PubMed (10 area queries, 6 journals; 5,646 hits, 4,611 unique records), ClinicalTrials.gov (908 records), the RCT-DUPLICATE list and a guideline hand search; one LLM screener. 161 eligible trials: 42% already in the pool (68/161); 97% recall of the pool's eligible trials (68/70); 38 new candidates in groups A–C (exploratory) and an infeasible group D. Not used for the current 38.

Designs and dates

New-user, active-comparator designs (time zero = first order of either drug, no comparator order in the prior 365 days); sequential add-on or switch designs where the trial tested adding or switching therapy against continuing it (e.g. rhythm control added to rate control; switching from warfarin). Outcome = the trial's primary endpoint. Index dates 2011–2024 (pipeline.md; paper). Note: the version 1 audit found COMET index dates extending into 2025.

Tiers (first rule that matches)

LimitedTotal ≥ 8; or N2 ≥ 2; or PP and (total − CO) ≥ 3; or SI = 2 because of an arm-assignment or time-zero error (until rebuilt and re-scored)
ModerateTotal 5–7; or N2 = 1 (any single item at 2 caps the tier at Moderate, whatever the total)
GoodTotal 3–4, with no item at 2
ExcellentTotal 0–2, with no item at 2

Sensitivity analysis only (primary: v19 tiers, A2). Analysed set = Excellent + Good + Moderate. Rescored on the spec-v2 cohorts: defects that the fixes removed are no longer penalised. An entry bound that the data can apply, and that spec v2 applies, scores 0. Tiers: 5 / 7 / 18 / 8.

Process and agreement

  • Two independent raters, blind to results, scored the trials from protocols, spec, code and data checks
  • Adjudication, then an independent audit (2 blocking findings: inconsistent unscored deviations; freeze conditions not met)
  • Rescored on the fixed cohorts; scores were hashed before any impact number was computed

Back to slide 10

Sensitivity analysis; the primary analysis uses the version 1 cohorts.

Five kinds of fix (patients removed; no index date moves)

  1. Published numeric entry bounds: HbA1c, BP, natriuretic peptides, cholesterol, renal and other labs; "unknown passes"
  2. Age bounds checked in all 38 (only CAROLINA removed anyone)
  3. Class washouts: other GLP-1RA, other SGLT2i, saxagliptin/alogliptin, prior ARNI, metoprolol succinate
  4. Gate fixes: LAAOS III AF before admission; LIFE definite LVH; COMET LVEF ≤35%; VALIANT LV dysfunction or HF
  5. Outcome rebuilds: AMPLIFY, LODESTAR, PROVE IT

Random-removal check (PS-CVD5 + ECG vs PS-CVD5, 54 items)

SetVersion 1Spec-v2Random removal, 20 draws: median (5th–95th pct)
Paper 1's 328.8%6.6%6.9 (2.8 to 9.3)
Provisional 299.4%6.5%6.9 (4.0 to 8.4)
All 389.0%6.7%7.0 (3.2 to 9.6)

Removing the same numbers of patients at random shrinks the gain just as much. So the drop from about 9% to 6.5% reflects refitting on smaller cohorts, not the fixes as such.

Not fixed (they need full rebuilds): CABANA (arm assignment) and TRANSFORM-HF (time zero); both stay scored. Six trials lost nobody.

Back to slide 12

10-01 → 10-09

  • Primary contrast: PS-CVD5 + ECG vs PS-CVD5 (paper 1: PS-Demo); fixed L2 penalty C = 1 for every PS; 1:1 matching, caliper 0.2.
  • Leakage audit: echo EF duplicates LVEF and eGFR derives from creatinine, so the primary panel is 54 non-coded items with leakage-corrected masking (58 items secondary).
  • PS-Clinical without LVEF (no PS contains any echo measurement), 5-draw multiple imputation.
  • R2 restart (branch r2): with a CV-tuned PS, PS-CVD5 + ECG fell to 4.7%, mostly from the CV penalty (8.6% at C = 1). Reverted to version 1, audited, hardened.
  • Explored: spec-v2 cohort fixes and emulation-quality framework v2.0.

10-09 → 10-13 (user decisions)

  • Primary back to version 1 cohorts and paper 1's 32 trials (v19 tiers). Decided after the fixed-cohort results were known (6.6% vs 8.8%): both are reported.
